items.title: Live: Economists won't rule out a further interest rate hike despite GDP slowdown
items.description: Australia's economy expanded 0.3 per cent in the first quarter of 2026, taking the annual growth rate to 2.5 per cent, the ABS says. Follow live.

items.title: Solomon Islands to begin treaty talks with Australia, review China pact
items.description: The new Solomon Islands prime minister has made a clear pivot towards Australia, agreeing to kickstart negotiations on a comprehensive treaty with Canberra and promising to "review" the Pacific nation's contentious security agreement with China.

items.title: Luke Sayers lewd photo fight to play out in open court
items.description: A bid by Mr Sayers to have a defamation case brought by his wife over a nude photo scandal heard privately has been rejected by a judge.

items.title: Iran launches ballistic missiles at American base as US hits Qeshm Island
items.description: The Revolutionary Guard says it has fired missiles and drones at US Fifth Fleet headquarters in Bahrain, while the US military has launched an attack on Qeshm Island.

items.title: 'Perverse logic' over abortion, Barnaby Joyce tells Sydney crowd
items.description: Nine months out from the NSW election campaign, One Nation recruit Barnaby Joyce has appeared in Sydney, declaring politicians are fearful of losing their jobs.

items.title: These are the 'worst offenders' in Australian packaging
items.description: A trendy plastic-and-metal takeaway cup used by cafes for iced drinks has been named Australia's worst packaging in the first Unpackit Awards.

items.title: Snowy 2.0 blows out by more than $3m a day. Will it ever be worth it?
items.description: Australia's most ambitious renewable energy project is slowly nearing completion, but experts are divided on whether Snowy 2.0 will ever justify its snowballing price tag.

items.title: Docker O'Driscoll says mental health admission 'best thing' he's done
items.description: Fremantle Dockers midfielder Nathan O'Driscoll says he has received "nothing but love" after posting on social media about his struggles with anxiety and how he contemplated taking his own life.

items.title: Former Canberra Liberals leader leaves party citing 'threat of physical assault'
items.description: Former Canberra Liberals leader Leanne Castley says she has experienced "bullying, intimidation, lies and a threat of physical assault" in the past 18 months.

items.title: Live: Marles says Australia wanted three second-hand subs all along
items.description: The defence minister says the new AUKUS deal that will see Australia buy three second-hand Virginia-class submarines from the US is what the government had wanted all along. Follow live.

items.title: Australian men guilty after taking 'black flight' to flee country
items.description: Three Australian men have been found guilty by a District Court in Merauke after taking a "black flight" into Indonesia's South Papua province from Far North Queensland without visas.

items.title: Kiwi greyhounds expected to be sent to Qld ahead of NZ racing ban
items.description: Australian officials say they will have no control over how the greyhounds are used once they arrive in Queensland.

items.title: Banned products in Australia sold on Temu, Amazon and AliExpresss
items.description: Products that may already be banned in Australia are being sold by retail giants including Amazon, Temu, AliExpress and eBay.

items.title: The housing 'super cycle' may be ending, and that could be a good thing
items.description: Before the federal budget, the housing market was already starting to choke on its own excesses. Now some economists are tipping an extended period where home prices grow no faster than general inflation.

items.title: Five ways to prevent mould in your home and the best ways to clean it
items.description: Winter is here and with it comes the increased risk of mould in homes, particularly in colder parts of the country. But there are simple ways to keep to it at bay.

items.title: This rapper was having panic attacks on stage, until he transitioned
items.description: Poet, rapper, musician, playwright and novelist Kae Tempest is a prodigious polymath. It wasn't until he affirmed his gender that he connected with his true self.

items.title: Why Hugh Jackman's brother cried on his first day as a prison-school teacher
items.description: After Ralph Jackman retrained as a teacher, his first job was in a youth detention centre. His new memoir reveals how a broken system is failing vulnerable kids.

items.title: 'Even sleep is expensive': The challenge for a people forced to live in ruins
items.description: It's been seven months since the ceasefire in Gaza, but reconstruction has barely begun, water remains contaminated and minimal aid is getting into the strip. This is what life is like for its residents.

items.title: Fertiliser imports hit one million tonne mark since Iran war began
items.description: Streamlined biosecurity checks of fertiliser shipments have fast-tracked imports of urea for Australia's winter crop.

items.title: Trump names inexperienced ally as intelligence director
items.description: Bill Pulte, who is known for publicly attacking the US president's political enemies, would also retain his existing jobs overseeing federal housing and mortgage policies.

items.title: Starmer condemns handcuffed teen's death as police response sparks protests
items.description: The British prime minister said he "felt sick" while watching video released by police of 18-year-old Henry Nowak, who was handcuffed while he lay dying from stab wounds after his killer falsely alleged a racist attack.

items.title: Heat-related deaths 'tip of the iceberg' in India as UN sends El Niño warning
items.description: India's deadly heatwave comes as the UN warns the world to prepare for a moderate to strong El Niño this year.

items.title: Peabo Bryson, A Whole New World and Beauty and the Beast singer, dies
items.description: Peabo Bryson, known for his Grammy and Oscar-winning Disney collaborations, has died at 75.

items.title: 'Us hunters': Victorian watchdog accused of siding with duck shooters
items.description: The Game Management Authority is accused of of turning a blind eye to illegal behaviour by shooters while bullying wildlife rescuers and anti-hunting campaigners.

items.title: 'Grossly negligent' UK Athletics fined for 'avoidable' death of Paralympian
items.description: Abdullah Hayayei, from the United Arab Emirates, was preparing for the 2017 World Paralympic Athletics Championships at the Newham Leisure Centre when a metal throwing cage fell on him.
